text:
Kai: Seeing a spike of OOMs in dedicated-gpu-3 around 10:15 UTC, correlated to long chat sessions (>12k tokens). KV heap keeps growing and never releases — looks like sticky slab fragments. Reprobed with a 50k-token convo and got OOM after ~9k more tokens.
Maria: ugh. any kernel selection changes rolled out recently? :thinking:
Kai: Not in the last week. We did a batching tweak yesterday but it targets short requests. This one looks like fragmentation + per-request KV retention.
Oleg: Can you paste the heap profile? even a short pprof summary helps.
Kai: paste below (stripped):
```
# pprof kv_heap 2025-11-12T10:17Z
Total: 7.8GiB
allocated_objects: 1.1M
Top by size:
  slab: 4.9GiB (62%)
  reused_cache: 1.3GiB (16%)
  misc: 1.6GiB (22%)
frag_ratio = slab / (slab + reused_cache) = 0.79
freelist_count low, hotspots in sequence_id ranges 4000-5200
```
Simon: frag_ratio ~0.8 is huge. That indicates large unusable holes between allocations. Sounds like per-sequence pinned caches that never compact.
Chloe: Can we flip a soft-mitigation? e.g., cap per-session kv retention size and enable periodic compaction sweep on the node?
Oleg: Proposed short-term fixes: 1) enable per-request kv cap 64MB 2) trigger opportunistic compaction at request end 3) mark old per-seq allocations as evictable (soft-evict) so they can be reclaimed before hard OOM.
Kai: I'm for that. Which one is lowest risk to prod?
Simon: (#2) opportunistic compaction is low-risk if throttled — do it during idle cycles only. Cap (1) will affect quality if we remove too much prefix. Soft-evict (3) needs runtime change + KV rehydration path.
infra-bot: Deploy pipeline triggered: release/kv-soft-evict-mitigations -> canary on dedicated-gpu-3 (1/3 nodes)
Maria: Also add alert: kv_frag_ratio > 0.6 sustained for 10m. Need a graph on console: kv_active_bytes, kv_frag_ratio, kv_free_chunks.
Chloe: Agreed. Also surface sequence-level retention metric: seq_kept_bytes{seq_id} so we can find offending sessions.
Oleg: Longer term: switch slab allocator to per-size-class coalescing, and add a compacting background thread that merges adjacent free ranges when fragmentation exceeds threshold. Also consider reuse-hot-cache separate pool (compact-friendly).
Kai: For immediate rollout: I'll enable per-request cap 64MB and opportunistic compaction (throttle=0.1) in canary. Simon, can you review the compaction throttle?
Simon: On it. Quick note: we should also add fallback policy in router: when node reports kv_frag_ratio>0.7, route new long contexts to small-quantized model instance or another region to avoid cascading OOM across nodes.
Maria: Good point — graceful degradation rules are important. Also make sure we record 'kv_eviction_count' in traces for every request so we can tie quality regressions to evictions.
Kai: After canary we saw one OOM on the other two nodes but canary node held. Pushing compaction throttle to 0.2 seems to help.
Chloe: Ran a quick perf/regression check on dev workload: average latency +3%, token cost -1% (less reallocation); no quality regressions in eyeballed prompts. :thumbsup:
Oleg: Follow-up tasks: A) instrument seq_kept_bytes metric B) add alert + dashboard C) design soft-evict rehydration path D) allocator coalescing RFC.
Kai: I'll open the RFCs and assign. For now rolling out to all dedicated nodes with 30m watch.
infra-bot: Canary finished: rollout to 2/3 nodes -> ok. Full rollout in 15m unless halted.
Simon: Add quick smoke: generate 20k-token synthetic convo and watch kv_active_bytes and frag_ratio. If frag_ratio doesn't drop post-evict compaction, revert.
Maria: Thanks everyone — once dashboards are live ping #product-alerts and SRE oncall.
Kai: Logging notes: added a small trace annotation on requests that trigger compaction: `kv.compaction=soft,throttle=0.2` for easier query.
Chloe: Nice. Let's validate after 24h and then plan RFC for allocator change. :rocket:
